<div id="pkg-content" style="display:none;">

  <div class="pkg-header">
    <h1>R Packages</h1>
    <p>Three R packages developed within the FunTraits toolkit for trait-based ecology of freshwater fish:
       from field photographs to landmarks, morphological traits, intraspecific variability and the global
       FISHMORPH morphospace. Click a package for its presentation page.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="my-grid">

    <a class="my-card" href="Rpackages_fishintrait.html">
      <div class="my-top">
        <div class="hex-sm" style="background:#27ae60;"><i class="fa fa-camera"></i></div>
        <div>
          <p class="my-name">FishInTrait</p>
          <span class="my-version">in development</span>
        </div>
      </div>
      <p class="my-tagline">Field-campaign management for trait digitization: photographs, specimens, determinations and provenance journal.</p>
      <ul class="my-feats">
        <li>Project layout shared with intraitR (photos · measurements · journal)</li>
        <li>Campaign journal recording the origin of every specimen</li>
        <li>Shiny explorer, incl. species absent from FISHMORPH</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="my-foot"><span class="gh"><i class="fa fa-github"></i> FunTraits</span><span class="arrow">Presentation →</span></div>
    </a>

    <a class="my-card" href="Rpackages_intraitr.html">
      <div class="my-top">
        <div class="hex-sm" style="background:#2980b9;"><i class="fa fa-crosshairs"></i></div>
        <div>
          <p class="my-name">intraitR</p>
          <span class="my-version">v1.35.0 · GitHub</span>
        </div>
      </div>
      <p class="my-tagline">Morphological trait analysis toolkit for freshwater fish — landmarks, Procrustes, ratios, shape and trait spaces, intraspecific variability and measurement error.</p>
      <ul class="my-feats">
        <li>Predictor-assisted landmark digitizer (Shiny + ml-morph)</li>
        <li>Landmark QC, GPA, allometry, trait and shape spaces</li>
        <li>ITV indices, repeatability, operator bias, FD inflation by ITV</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="my-foot"><span class="gh"><i class="fa fa-github"></i> FunTraits/intraitR</span><span class="arrow">Presentation →</span></div>
    </a>

    <a class="my-card" href="Rpackages_rfishmorph.html">
      <div class="my-top">
        <div class="hex-sm" style="background:#c0392b;"><i class="fa fa-database"></i></div>
        <div>
          <p class="my-name">Rfishmorph</p>
          <span class="my-version">v0.13.1 · GitHub</span>
        </div>
      </div>
      <p class="my-tagline">Digitizing, storing, analysing and exploring the FISHMORPH database (Brosse et al. 2021): 21 landmarks, 11 segments, 9 ratios.</p>
      <ul class="my-feats">

  <div class="section-title">How they fit together</div>
  <div class="flow">
    <div class="flow-box"><b>FishInTrait</b>campaign · photographs · provenance</div>
    <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
    <div class="flow-box"><b>intraitR</b>landmarks → traits → ITV &amp; measurement error</div>
    <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
    <div class="flow-box"><b>Rfishmorph</b>FISHMORPH scheme · global morphospace · database</div>
  </div>
  <p class="section-text">The three packages share the same object classes (<code>intrait_landmarks</code> is accepted
  throughout) and the same FISHMORPH conventions, so a survey digitized with FishInTrait can be analysed with intraitR
  and projected into — or added to — the FISHMORPH database with Rfishmorph. <code>intraitR</code> imports
  <code>Rfishmorph</code>; both build on <code>geomorph</code> for geometric morphometrics.</p>

  <div class="section-title">Installation</div>
  <div class="install-section">
<pre><code># install.packages("remotes")
install.packages("geomorph")
remotes::install_github("FunTraits/Rfishmorph")
remotes::install_github("FunTraits/intraitR")     # pulls Rfishmorph automatically</code></pre>
  </div>


  <div class="section-title" id="students">For students: from photographs to results</div>
  <div class="student-section">
    <p class="student-intro">If you join a digitization campaign with me, you receive a folder of <strong>prepared
    photographs</strong> (one specimen per file, exported from the campaign project with FishInTrait; the file name is the
    specimen code and must not be changed). Install the packages as above, then follow the two steps below. Photographs
    never leave your computer: only their file name and pixel size are recorded.</p>

    <div class="student-step">
      <div class="student-num">1</div>
      <div class="student-body">
        <h3>Measure the specimens and send the measurements back</h3>
        <p>Create a working folder with the photographs in <code>prepared/</code> and launch the digitizer. From a few
        calibration clicks, the ml-morph predictor proposes the 19 FISHMORPH landmarks; review every point, place the
        scale bar (landmarks 20–21, length in mm asked by the app), score the quality and save. Everything is written
        to <strong>one workbook</strong> and to an <strong>append-only journal</strong> that survives a crash.</p>
        <p>Not comfortable with R? The <a href="#app">pipeline app</a> opens this same digitizer in your browser and
        hands you the same workbook and journal to send back — no installation at all.</p>
<pre><code>library(intraitR)

digitize_landmarks(
  photo_dir   = "prepared",                          # the photographs I gave you
  xlsx_path   = "measurements/&lt;Name&gt;_landmarks.xlsx", # one workbook, 3 sheets
  journal_dir = "journal",                           # source of truth, never edit
  operator    = "&lt;your initials&gt;",
  mode        = "new"                                # "correct" to review, "repeat" for repeatability
)

# Optional but recommended: digitize ~20 specimens 3 times blind for the
# measurement-error analysis (mode = "repeat" fills the "bias" sheet).</code></pre>
        <p>When you are done, send me a zip of the <strong>workbook and the <code>journal/</code> folder</strong>
        (the workbook alone is an export; the journal is what I merge into the campaign project
        <code>00_CampagneIntrait</code> with <code>consolidate_landmarks()</code>). Please do not edit the workbook by hand,
        do not rename photographs, and keep the same <code>operator</code> code from start to end.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="student-step">
      <div class="student-num">2</div>
      <div class="student-body">
        <h3>Analyse and visualise your data</h3>
        <p>Read the workbook back, check the landmarks on the photographs, correct the geometry, derive the FISHMORPH
        traits, then explore trait space, shape space, intraspecific variability and your own repeatability.</p>
<pre><code>library(intraitR)

# ── read the measurements sheet (wide layout written by the digitizer) ────────
fish &lt;- read_landmarks_xlsx("measurements/&lt;Name&gt;_landmarks.xlsx",
                            sheet = "measurements", n_landmarks = 23,
                            x_pattern = "{i}_X", y_pattern = "{i}_Y",
                            id_cols = "specimen")
# species come from the determinations table I give you (uid, species, ...),
# never from the file name: the specimen code SITE_YYYYMMDD_NNNN is an identity,
# the species a revisable hypothesis
det     &lt;- read.csv("determinations.csv")
uid     &lt;- sub("_i[0-9]+$", "", fish$metadata$specimen)   # drop the _iK of plates
species &lt;- det$species[match(uid, det$uid)]

# ── quality control ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plot_fishmorph_points(fish, specimen = 1,
                      background_image = "prepared/&lt;code&gt;.jpg")   # points on the photo
fish &lt;- impute_landmarks(fish)              # missing point (e.g. LM5) estimated
fish &lt;- standardize_orientation(fish)       # head left, belly down
fish &lt;- correct_geometry(fish)              # FISHMORPH digitizing conventions
detect_outliers(fish)

# ── FISHMORPH traits: 11 segments → 9 ratios ────────────────────────────────
seg &lt;- fishmorph_segments(fish)             # cm, via the scale bar
rat &lt;- fishmorph_ratios(seg)
summary_traits(rat, groups = species)

# ── functional trait space of your sample ────────────────────────────────────
fts &lt;- trait_space(rat, groups = species, na_action = "omit", remove_outliers = TRUE)
plot(fts)                                   # spider / ellipse per species
plot(fts, style = "hull")
trait_disparity(rat, groups = species)      # do species differ in trait dispersion?

# ── your specimens in the global FISHMORPH morphospace (9 556 species) ───────
proj &lt;- project_fishmorph(rat, groups = species)
plot(proj, style = "hull")                  # density of the database + your species
plot(proj, style = "spider", itv_reference = TRUE)

# ── intraspecific variability ────────────────────────────────────────────────
itv &lt;- itv_index(rat, groups = species)     # inter- vs intraspecific variance
itv; plot(itv)
plot(itv_accumulation(rat, groups = species))   # how many individuals are enough?

# ── shape space (geometric morphometrics) ────────────────────────────────────
gpa &lt;- gpa_fish(fishmorph_shape_landmarks(fish))
ss  &lt;- shape_space(gpa, groups = species)
plot(ss)
intraspecific_variability(gpa, groups = species, traits = rat)

# ── your repeatability (if you used mode = "repeat") ─────────────────────────
rep &lt;- read_landmarks_xlsx("measurements/&lt;Name&gt;_landmarks.xlsx",
                           sheet = "bias", n_landmarks = 23,
                           x_pattern = "{i}_X", y_pattern = "{i}_Y",
                           id_cols = c("individual", "operator", "replicate"))
measurement_error(rep, individual = rep$metadata$individual)
plot(digitization_error(rep, individual = rep$metadata$individual))   # bias per landmark</code></pre>
        <div class="callout">
          A complete worked example on real field data, with the same steps, ships with the package:
          <code>demo("pipeline_T26_saudrune", package = "intraitR")</code>, and the vignette
          <code>vignette("intraitR-intro")</code> explains each function. Keep your analysis in a script
          (or an R Markdown file) so that it can be re-run when I return the consolidated campaign data.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>


  <div class="section-title" id="app">No R? Use the pipeline app</div>
  <div class="app-card">
    <div class="app-icon"><i class="fa fa-mouse-pointer"></i></div>
    <div class="app-body">
      <h3>intraitR pipeline — point-and-click</h3>
      <p>The whole workflow in a web application, for people who do not write R: measure the landmarks on your
      photographs, check and correct them, compute the FISHMORPH traits, and get the figures (trait space, FISHMORPH
      morphospace, intraspecific variability, shape space, repeatability) with every table and the R script that
      reproduces them. Every computation is an <code>intraitR</code> function, and the measuring step
      <strong>is the package's own digitizer</strong> — the application behind <code>digitize_landmarks()</code>,
      served as it is, so it writes the same workbook and the same append-only journal.</p>
      <div class="app-steps">
        <span>1 Start</span><span>2 Measure</span><span>3 Check</span><span>4 Traits</span><span>5 Trait space</span>
        <span>6 FISHMORPH</span><span>7 ITV</span><span>8 Shape</span><span>9 Repeatability</span><span>10 Export</span>
      </div>
    </div>

</div>

<script>
const CORRECT_HASH = "ac95cc34e3ff9d4e59fd3066f6feaee0d2f4f7f97d3865148bc5767834883ff5";

async function sha256(msg) {
  const buf = await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", new TextEncoder().encode(msg));
  return Array.from(new Uint8Array(buf)).map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2,"0")).join("");
}

function unlock() {
  document.getElementById("pw-overlay").style.display = "none";
  document.getElementById("pkg-content").style.display = "block";
  sessionStorage.setItem("rpackages_unlocked", "1");
}

async function checkPw() {
  const hash = await sha256(document.getElementById("pw-input").value);
  if (hash === CORRECT_HASH) {
    unlock();
  } else {
    const err = document.getElementById("pw-error");
    err.textContent = "Incorrect password. Please try again.";
    document.getElementById("pw-input").value = "";
    document.getElementById("pw-input").focus();
    setTimeout(() => { err.textContent = ""; }, 3000);
  }
}

if (sessionStorage.getItem("rpackages_unlocked") === "1" ||
    sessionStorage.getItem("rscripts_unlocked") === "1") {
  unlock();
}

</script>
